questions.q: What is the main advantage of preventive servicing according to the owner's handbook?
options: It makes checking the tyres unnecessary
It catches and treats problems before they become expensive or dangerous
It removes the need for the periodic vehicle test
It is always given for free
questions.explain: Preventive servicing catches a problem early and cheaply; repairing it after a breakdown is more expensive and sometimes more dangerous.

questions.q: Who decides the exact service intervals (in km and months) for a car?
options: The vehicle manufacturer's handbook
The Israel Police
The insurance company
Each garage decides for itself
questions.explain: The vehicle manufacturer sets the exact service intervals in the owner's handbook, based on the components and the engine.

questions.q: What causes service intervals to be shortened?
options: Driving in harsh conditions — dust, heat, towing, short trips
Washing the car often
Changing the radio
Driving only on a expressway
questions.explain: Harsh driving conditions place more load on the engine and components, and so shorten the recommended service intervals.

questions.q: When do you check the engine oil level on the dipstick?
options: Right after driving, while the engine is hot and running
While driving
With the engine switched off for a few minutes and the car on level ground
At any speed, regardless of the car's condition
questions.explain: An accurate check needs the engine off for a few minutes (so the oil drains back into the sump) and the car standing on level ground.

questions.q: When is it safe to check the coolant in the expansion tank?
options: Only when the engine is cold
Only right after a long journey
Only when the engine is hot and running
In any condition, it makes no difference
questions.explain: When the engine is hot the coolant is boiling and under pressure; opening the cap can cause severe burns.

questions.q: What does a marked drop in the brake fluid level indicate?
options: Advanced pad wear or a leak — check it soon
A natural effect you can ignore
Excess humidity in the air
A fault in the air conditioning
questions.explain: A marked drop in brake fluid is a warning sign of advanced pad wear or a leak, and needs an immediate check.

questions.q: What is it recommended to check once a week around the car?
options: Tyres, lights and washer fluid
The seat height
The gearbox oil level only
The air pressure in the air conditioning
questions.explain: A short weekly check of the tyres, lights and washer fluid catches common problems before they turn into a breakdown on the road.

questions.q: What is the role of the engine's air filter?
options: To warm the incoming air
To clean the air in the passenger cabin
To stop dust and sand getting into the engine
To filter fuel before the injectors
questions.explain: The air filter stops dust and sand getting into the engine; when it's clogged, it hurts performance and fuel consumption.

questions.q: What happens in most engines if the timing belt snaps while driving?
options: Only the air conditioning stops working
The car keeps driving normally with no problem
The engine automatically shifts to neutral only
The valves and pistons can collide, causing serious damage to the engine
questions.explain: In most engines, a snapped timing belt causes the valves and pistons to collide — serious damage that costs as much as a new engine.

questions.q: When is a timing belt replaced?
options: By kilometres or years as set by the vehicle manufacturer, whichever comes first — not when you sense a problem
Only when the car won't start
It never needs replacing
Only when you hear a squealing noise
questions.explain: A timing belt usually snaps without any prior warning, so it is replaced on a fixed schedule, not by feel.

questions.q: What does the cabin filter stop?
options: Dust, soot and pollen before they enter the passenger cabin
Metal particles from the engine oil
Water from the fuel filter
Exhaust pollution only
questions.explain: The cabin filter cleans the air entering the air conditioning and blower, of dust, soot and pollen.

questions.q: What significantly shortens the life of a 12V battery?
options: Regular engine oil changes
Long, regular trips
Only short trips and extreme heat
Moderate temperature all year round
questions.explain: Short trips don't fully recharge the battery, and extreme heat dries out the electrolyte inside it.

questions.q: How long does a typical 12V battery usually last in a private car?
options: It has no defined lifespan
About a month only
About twenty years
About three to five years
questions.explain: A typical battery in a private car lasts about three to five years, after which it is worth checking at every service.

questions.q: Why might a car left standing for weeks without driving end up with a flat battery?
options: This never actually happens
Because the car's computer systems constantly draw a small current, even when the car is off
Because the battery heats itself up
Because the law requires disconnecting the battery every week
questions.explain: The car's computer systems keep drawing a small current even with the engine off, and over weeks this drains the battery.

questions.q: What is true about handling a battery?
options: It contains acid and flammable hydrogen gas, and needs care
It's fine to bring a flame near it
It's fine to tilt it without limit
It contains no hazardous substances at all
questions.explain: A battery contains acid and flammable hydrogen gas; avoid flames, sparks, and tilting it.

questions.q: A new private car, first registered from 1 January 2023 — when does it undergo its first periodic vehicle test?
options: After one year
After only {{fact:vehicletest.private.interval_years}}
Immediately upon registration
After {{fact:vehicletest.private.first_test_years}} from first registration
questions.explain: A new private car is exempt from the periodic vehicle test for {{fact:vehicletest.private.first_test_years}} from first registration (reg. 273(b2)(1)).

questions.q: What does a car receive after passing the periodic vehicle test?
options: A new driving licence
A permanent exemption from future tests
A roadworthiness stamp on the vehicle licence
An exemption from compulsory insurance
questions.explain: The vehicle test examiner stamps the vehicle licence with a roadworthiness stamp when the car meets all the requirements.

questions.q: What is the default validity period of an ordinary vehicle licence?
options: Five years
Six months
{{fact:vehiclelicence.validity}}
For life
questions.explain: Regulation 276(a): the validity of a vehicle licence or its renewal is {{fact:vehiclelicence.validity}}, unless set otherwise.

questions.q: Which of these is included in the periodic vehicle test?
options: Checking average fuel consumption
Brakes, steering, tyres, lights, emissions and the condition of the bodywork
Checking the maximum speed on a expressway
Checking theory-test scores
questions.explain: The periodic vehicle test checks the car's main safety and emissions systems — not the driver's knowledge or performance.

questions.q: What is worth checking before trusting a garage?
options: A business licence, transparent pricing, and showing old parts on request
Only that the garage is open at weekends
Only the size of the sign outside
Only the colour of the walls
questions.explain: A valid licence, an up-front quote, and showing replaced parts are all signs of a trustworthy, transparent garage.

questions.q: What is the difference between an original part and an aftermarket part?
options: An original part is made or approved by the vehicle manufacturer; an aftermarket part is made by another company
An aftermarket part is always better
An original part is always cheaper
There is no difference at all
questions.explain: An aftermarket part is made by a company other than the vehicle manufacturer; its quality ranges from identical to the original to inferior.

questions.q: What is a safety recall?
options: A promotional campaign by the importer
A notice from the manufacturer or importer about a safety defect in a particular model, with a free repair
A requirement to re-insure the car
A fine for missing a service
questions.explain: A safety recall is a notice about a defect found in a particular model, with a free repair at an authorised garage.
